mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the federal funds rate above 4.0% combined with elevated CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL > 300) signals aggressive monetary tightening that increases equity discount rates and reduces risk appetite, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 4.0 and CPIAUCSL > 300.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate exceeding 4.0% indicates a restrictive monetary policy environment that suppresses equity valuations through higher discount rates, generating negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >60% of periods where FEDFUNDS > 4.0.

mechanism_narrative: Robust payroll growth (PAYEMS > 154,000) combined with low unemployment (UNRATE < 4%) reflects strong labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in >60% of instances where PAYEMS > 154000 and UNRATE < 4.0.

failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in >60% of periods where GDPC1 > 22125 and HOUST > 1400.
